LESSON: RELATIONS WITH PEOPLE OF OTHER FAITHS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Muamalaat (Social Relations)
Topic 6.2: Relations with people of other faiths
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Relations with people of other faiths, part of Muamalaat (Social Relations) in Grade 6 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: How should Muslims relate with people of other faiths? 2. What are the rights of the people of other faiths?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. research on the rights of non-Muslims from available reference materials and make class presentation,

2. discuss ways of living peacefully with non- Muslims and display on a chart (Q., 2:256, 8:61, 60:8, 109:6),

3. role- play ways of living harmoniously with people of other faiths. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. research on the rights of non-Muslims from available reference materials and make class presentation,
2. discuss ways of living peacefully with non- Muslims and display on a chart (Q., 2:256, 8:61, 60:8, 109:6),
3. role- play ways of living harmoniously with people of other faiths. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Relations with people of other faiths together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: listening, speaking, writing and teamwork skills heightened through group discussions

and presentation

• Creativity and Imagination: networking attained as they role-play ways of living peacefully with non-Muslims.

Values:
• Respect: there is open-mindedness as learners make presentations on the rights of non-Muslims.

• Peace: compassion developed in learners as they discuss ways of living peacefully with non-Muslims.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: Social cohesion and human rights enhanced as learners learn to co-exist with people of diverse faiths.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Social Studies: it has some aspects of harmonious living.
